headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: uptrend holds; Binance reserve news helps, price stays soft

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's budget posture is still to scale up acquisition: the long-run uptrend is intact, and this kind of phase has historically been when spending to win new and returning users paid back best, especially among active traders. This week calls for applying it carefully: Binance says about 95% of the affected assets are replaced and money leaving it has slowed, but its wider reserve check is still to come, a second exchange is still paused after a security incident, price is about 5% under its 50-day average, and the mood is fearful. So add spend in small steps, lead with safety and trust rather than hard offers, and speed up only once price wins back about $81,965. This is a budget-timing guide for the business, not trading advice.

reasons: BTC ($77,970) is about 7% above its 200-day average ($73,170), which is still rising.
Up about 22% over 90 days; about 84% of those days closed above the long-term average.
But price has closed under its 50-day average ($81,965) for 12 days, about 5% below it.
Money leaving Binance has slowed to about $3.5 billion a day; Fear & Greed is 37 (fear).
watch: The long-run trend still points up, but price has spent 12 days under its 50-day average even as the Binance news improves, and the mood is still fearful. A close above $79,500 would steady things, while a close below $77,369 puts the $73,170 average in focus.
analysis: Bottom line: the long-run uptrend still holds and the Binance worry keeps easing, but prices have not recovered yet. Short term is soft to neutral: Bitcoin has closed under its 50-day average for 12 days, sits about 5% below it and about 10% under its 30-day high, and the mood still reads fear (37 out of 100). Money leaving Binance has slowed, from about $7 billion a day at its peak to about $3.5 billion (DefiLlama via PANews), while Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin is still paused after its own security incident, saying customers were not affected. A normal week now swings about $2,926, so a close above $79,500 (top of a typical week's swing) would turn it clearly up, a close below $77,369 (the 30-day low) would turn it down, and in between it stays choppy. A clean result from Binance's wider 4 November check would help the mood and another exchange incident would hurt it, so keep leading with trust rather than offers.

The next month is mixed. The 90-day numbers still point up, with price about 22% higher, but the last 30 days are down about 8%, and October was one of Bitcoin's weakest Octobers on record (CoinGlass via PANews). Price must win back $81,965 (the 50-day average) for the month to firm up, and it only has room to climb above $86,603 (the 90-day high); while it stays under that average, the month keeps fading. This week brings the US midterm elections on 3 November, the US jobs report on 6 November and the start of Brazilian banks blocking unlicensed crypto firms the same day, and the next Fed meeting is 8 December. Save bigger campaign pushes for that reclaim.

The 3-6 month picture still leans up at a moderate strength. Price is about 7% above its 200-day average and that average is still rising, about 3% over 90 days, though Bitcoin remains about 38% below its all-time high. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $73,170 (the 200-day average); if that goes, $67,216 (the 200-week average) is the next floor, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. So far the largest crypto theft on record has not broken this picture, and a close below the 200-day average is what would weaken it, which would be the moment to move budget toward keeping existing users.

items.theme: Exchanges race to show their reserves
items.why: Binance says about 95% of the assets hit in the hack are replaced and has opened a tool for users to check ten major coins, with a wider snapshot planned for 4 November. OKX published its 49th reserve report the same day. Money leaving Binance has slowed to about $3.5 billion a day from a peak near $7 billion per DefiLlama, and deposits are back to about 78% of withdrawals.
items.marketing_angle: A timely education topic: what a reserve report proves and what it does not.

BTCPay Server says versions up to 2.4.1 were targeted and has no credible reports of theft on the latest version.

items.headline: Binance: ZK Proof for Oct. 31 Reserve Snapshot Generated, Asset Replenishment Reaches 95%
items.why: Binance says about 95% of the affected assets have been replaced and users can now check that ten major coins are backed at least one-to-one, which answers the biggest open question since the hack; this is the company's own statement.

items.why: Most crypto firms in Brazil did not apply to keep operating and banks start blocking unlicensed firms from 6 November, which narrows access in one large market.

items.why: A major market's regulator is pushing exchanges to keep more funds offline and hold extra reserves, a small plus for trust, though it adds cost for exchanges.

items.why: Fifty listed companies now object to their shares trading in token form on the OKX and ICE platform, a setback for one of the sector's main growth stories.

items.headline: HKMA: Ensemble TX achieves round-the-clock real transactions in tokenised deposits, plans expansion to regulated stablecoins
items.why: Hong Kong's central bank moving real money on token rails around the clock, with regulated stablecoins next, is another step toward mainstream finance using this technology.

summary.short: Binance's reserve proof and 95% replacement ease the main worry, partly offset by a new incident at Mercado Bitcoin.
summary.medium: Brazil's licensing squeeze and pushback on tokenized shares slightly outweigh tighter custody rules in South Korea.
summary.long: Hong Kong's round-the-clock tokenised deposits are a small positive for mainstream use.
